source_of_truth: Operator direction 2026-06-11 (worktree-isolation-v0 D012 split): own the enforcement half of worktree isolation — plan-mutating commands refuse from the wrong worktree unless explicitly overridden with durable evidence, and cleanup is health-gated, audit-first, explicit, and never force-deletes — built on v0's canonical binding_health predicate, with the COMPLETE guard/cleanup threat model pinned in one pre-lock design pass (corrupt registry fail-closed, canonical path comparison, swapped-repo defense, override evidence durability, create-rollback/audit-first ordering, and the operator's explicit decision on gitignored-file semantics in cleanup).
completion_test: Every plan-mutating entry point (lock, audit, close, disposition, orchestrate dispatch) refuses fail-closed on wrong worktree, corrupt registry, or any failed binding_health conjunct, naming the reason; an override with a reason proceeds ONLY after the override record and binding snapshot are durably written; `plan worktree remove` removes only a healthy, clean (per the design-pass-decided contract semantics) binding, audit-entry-first, with no force path anywhere; plan close never auto-removes; all proven by fixture tests per conjunct and per entry point with zero live auditor calls.

user_journeys.name: wrong-worktree-guard
user_journeys.description: A session in the wrong checkout (or against a corrupt registry, or a swapped repository at the recorded path) tries a plan-mutating command and is refused with the failed conjunct; an explicit override durably records evidence then proceeds.

user_journeys.name: safe-cleanup
user_journeys.description: Operator removes a finished plan's worktree; unhealthy or unclean state refuses with reasons; eligible removal is audited before anything is deleted.
